classification.difficultyReason: Restrict the radical domain, compare a semicircle with an absolute-value graph, and retain an isolated equality point.

inlines.text: Compare the graphs on the radical's domain

answer.worked:
The radical is defined for $0\le x\le4$. Its graph is the upper semicircle $y=\sqrt{4-(x-2)^2}$. On this domain, $|x|=x$, so compare the semicircle with $y=x$.
At their intersections,
$$\begin{align*}x^2&=4x-x^2\\2x^2&=4x\\2x(x-2)&=0\\x&=0\text{ or }2.\end{align*}$$
The line is on or above the semicircle at $x=0$ and throughout $2\le x\le4$. Thus $x=0$ or $2\le x\le4$.

spec.description: Upper semicircle centred at (2,0), compared with the absolute-value function on the radical's domain.
spec.mathematics: Radical domain [0,4]; comparison intersections (0,0) and (2,2). The required set is {0} union [2,4].
